adjudicated.jp: 「その息子ってのが、豊なんだよな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "That son was, of course, Yutaka."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.
The source text has multiple authoritative occurrences and this unit lacks a unique binding.

adjudicated.jp: 霧は反応できていなかった。
adjudicated.en: Kiri was unable to react.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 手の震えは止まっていた。
adjudicated.en: The shaking of her hands stopped.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 落ち着いた……わけではなかった。
adjudicated.en: Calming down... was not the cause.
adjudicated.assessment: The stillness does not mean that Kiri has calmed down. 'Was not the cause' treats calming as a cause rather than a rejected interpretation.

highlights.text: Calming down... was not the cause.

adjudicated.jp: 愕然とした表情で、俺を見ている。
adjudicated.en: Terror in her facial expression, she looks at me.
adjudicated.assessment: 愕然 describes a stunned or shocked expression. 'Terror' identifies fear rather than shocked disbelief.

highlights.text: Terror in her facial expression, she looks at me.

adjudicated.jp: 矢尻が俺からそれていることも、気づいていない。
adjudicated.en: She hadn't noticed that the tip of the bolt had strayed from me.
comments: Arrow + butt = tip of the bolt. I don't actually know if it's called an arrowhead regardless. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「で、読めてたかも知れないけど、Ｓってのは新川のイニシャルでもあった」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "And, as you maybe have guessed, 'S' is also the initial of Shinkawa."
comments: ...which makes it plausible there'd be plays on names (and perhaps more) where more than the kanji or the kana changes, but also Western romanizations being changed by single letters. In other words, it is perfectly valid to think a Youko/Touko association despite changes in only a letter, rather than a whole kana or kanji. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……な、なにを言って……？」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...wh-, what did you say...?"
adjudicated.assessment: Kiri asks what Taichi is saying now. 'What did you say?' asks for repetition of a completed utterance.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...wh-, what did you say...?"

adjudicated.jp: 半笑い。
adjudicated.en: Half smile.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 感情さえコントロールできていない様子。
adjudicated.en: She is unable to keep even emotions under control.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「あいつも子供なのにあんなこと知っちゃってさ。もうまともな人生にはならないって思ってたよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Guy's a child, but he's well acquainted with that stuff. I thought he'd never be able to have a proper life anymore."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「末は変態かジャンキーかってさ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "He'd end up as a pervert or maybe a junkie."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「嘘だっっ！！」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "YOU LIE!!!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 金切り声。
adjudicated.en: Piercing loud scream.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「嘘だ、嘘だ嘘だ嘘だ！！　嘘つかないでよ！　気でも狂ったの！？　そんなでまかせ……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "You lie, you lie you LIE YOU LIE!!! Don't lie to me! Did you lose your mind?! You're just spreading garbage..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「事実だよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "It's the truth."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 再び霧の手は震え出す。
adjudicated.en: Once again Kiri's hands began shaking.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「そんなことあるわけない！　豊がそんなことしていたはずがない！」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "That simply can't be! It's simply impossible that Yutaka would ever do anything like that!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「そんなことあるし、豊はそんなことをしていた」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "That simply is. Yutaka did all that."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「一番張り切ってたぞ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "And he was the most enthusiastic!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 笑う。
adjudicated.en: I laugh.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「まあ子供だから、大人の女を強姦するってのはきつかったんだろうな。アソコだって子供にはショックの大きな―――」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, and he was a kid, so raping adult females has gotta have been harsh. To a child, those privates would a big shock that's---"
comments: 強姦 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「黙って！！」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "SILENCE!!!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 張り裂けそうな声。
adjudicated.en: Her voice seems to be bursting open.
adjudicated.assessment: Her voice sounds ready to split or tear. 'Bursting open' is an unnatural physical description of a voice.

highlights.text: Her voice seems to be bursting open.

adjudicated.jp: 「そんな話、聞いたこともない！　ずっと暮らしてきて、そんな話があったなんて。ありえない……考えられない―――」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "I have never heard about this anywhere! We've always lived together, and he never talked about that. Impossible... unthinkable---"
comments: Already from the voice it's obvious she suspects. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Kiri says that despite living together all that time, she never heard that such a story existed. The English specifically says that Yutaka never told her, assigning the silence to him.

highlights.text: Kiri: "I have never heard about this anywhere! We've always lived together, and he never talked about that. Impossible... unthinkable---"

adjudicated.jp: 「記憶喪失」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Memory loss."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ぴたりと霧は口をつぐんだ。
adjudicated.en: Kiri's lips closed tight on the spot.
adjudicated.assessment: ぴたり conveys that Kiri stops speaking abruptly. 'On the spot' instead describes location or immediacy of action.

highlights.text: Kiri's lips closed tight on the spot.

adjudicated.jp: 名探偵になった気分だ。
adjudicated.en: It felt she had become a detective, and a great one.
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi feels like a great detective. The English says that Kiri has become one.

highlights.text: It felt she had become a detective, and a great one.

adjudicated.jp: 「謎はとけまくってんだよ、霧ちん」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "So you have unraveled the mystery, Kiri-chin."
comments: He's still being an ass. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi boasts that the mystery is unraveling all over or practically solving itself. The English credits Kiri with unraveling it.

highlights.text: Taichi: "So you have unraveled the mystery, Kiri-chin."

adjudicated.jp: 「……それは……記憶がないのは……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...that is... he has no memories of it and..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「あと俺、あいつがどうして脚を怪我したのか知ってる」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "And, I know why that guy's leg is injured."
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi knows how Yutaka injured his leg. 'Why that guy's leg is injured' asks for a present condition rather than the cause of the injury event.

highlights.text: Taichi: "And, I know why that guy's leg is injured."

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...eh?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「その場にいたからな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Because I was there."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……じゃあ……先輩は……それを知ってて？」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...then... Senpai... you knew he...?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「いんにゃ？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Nyope."
comments: Fukuoka-ben. Cats will be fine, too. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「俺は豊が生き延びたなんて思ってなかったし……豊って名前も忘れてたよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I never thought that Yutaka would still be around... I forgot the very name Yutaka."
comments: MEMORY HUNTER! Yutaka came to Kamisaka when Taichi was halfway through his first year, around one or two years after Taichi did. Utterly ridiculous he'd have forgotten the guy who had spearheaded his torture for weeks, perhaps months, and that he thought he had killed so ferociously. Of course, see CCA0011C: like hell he's forgotten. This is a hint that while Taichi remembers, he doesn't necessarily Remember. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……あいつと出会ったのは偶然だ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...meeting him was a coincidence."
comments: Of the same kind that'll be seen in Miki's route. This is pure Providence. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「俺も女装させられてたし……向こうもわからなかったみたいだけど」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I had been put into girls' clothing so... looks like there wasn't any recognizing from him either."
adjudicated.assessment: Because Taichi was cross-dressed, Yutaka apparently did not recognize him either. 'There wasn't any recognizing from him' is ungrammatical and obscures the object of recognition.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I had been put into girls' clothing so... looks like there wasn't any recognizing from him either."

adjudicated.jp: だが豊は生き残った。
adjudicated.en: For all that, Yutaka had survived.
comments: Readers still don't know Yutaka should've died. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「でまあ、いろいろあって俺も解放されて……紆余曲折あってここに来たわけだけど」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "So well, lots of complications and I was set free... there were lots of twists and turns and I ended up here."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「考えてみれば当然だよな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Thinking back, it's just natural, isn't it."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「豊も俺も、あれで心が壊れないはずないんだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "There was no way that that wouldn't break our spirits, nor for me nor for Yutaka."
adjudicated.assessment: The paired negative requires 'neither for Yutaka nor for me,' not 'nor for me nor for Yutaka.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "There was no way that that wouldn't break our spirits, nor for me nor for Yutaka."

adjudicated.jp: 「出会うのは必然だったのかな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I wonder if us meeting was just inevitable."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……そんな……残酷な人じゃない……信じられない」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...but he's... not that cruel a person... I'll never believe this!"
comments: Going by how she treats in CCC3004, it's possible that she figured out exactly what kind of person he was, whether she accepted it or not. Then again, she's not the smartest or hardest to convince. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「豊のことに気づいたのは、親しくなったあとだよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I recognized Yutaka after we got close."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……だから……殺した？」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...that's why... you murdered him?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ま、もうごまかしはきかないだろう。
adjudicated.en: Well, seems deceptions won't work anymore.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 俺も、吐き出したくなった。
adjudicated.en: I, too, just wanted to spit it out.
comments: This reads as if he wants to just state outright his hatred for him... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「すぐに殺意がわいたわけじゃない」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "It's not like I immediately fired into some murderous rage."
comments: ...but he doesn't. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「過去のことだしな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "It was just a thing of the past."
comments: It's both true and false. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「だったら……！」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "But then...!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 流れが逆転しはじめていた。
adjudicated.en: The flow began to reverse.
comments: Pshaw, this requires at least seventeen more twists, none of which make any sense (though some of which are certainly awesome). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 感情のうねりは打ち寄せた波、俺を湿らせて引き返していく。
adjudicated.en: The wave of her swelling emotions had broken ashore, drenched me, and is now withdrawing.
adjudicated.assessment: The wave had already broken and was withdrawing. The English shifts from past perfect to present progressive within the same completed observation.

highlights.text: The wave of her swelling emotions had broken ashore, drenched me, and is now withdrawing.

adjudicated.jp: 霧。
adjudicated.en: Kiri...
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: アタックしてきたのは、おまえの方なんだからな。
adjudicated.en: She had gone on the attack because that is her way.
adjudicated.assessment: The speaker says that the addressee was the one who came at or attacked him first. The English assigns the attack to a third-person woman and turns the reason into her general disposition.

highlights.text: She had gone on the attack because that is her way.

adjudicated.jp: 「苦しんでいるのなら、見逃してやろうと思った」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I thought, if he's in pain, I'll let it go."
comments: See CCC3007, it's possible he was already aware then. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The speaker recounts his earlier thought that he would let the matter go if the other person was suffering too. 'I'll let it go' changes that embedded past intention into a present promise.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I thought, if he's in pain, I'll let it go."

adjudicated.jp: 「けど俺とつるんでいる時のあいつは、幸せそうだった」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But when he was hanging around with me, he seemed to be happy."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

comments: HACK independent doll shake -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「あの日……わたしに質問した……幸せかって……？」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "That day... you asked me... was he happy...?"
adjudicated.assessment: The quoted question asks the speaker whether the speaker was happy. The English instead asks whether an absent male was happy.

highlights.text: Kiri: "That day... you asked me... was he happy...?"

adjudicated.jp: 「よく覚えてるな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You remember that, good."
adjudicated.assessment: 'You remember that, good' is an ungrammatical splice and does not cleanly express the approving reaction to the addressee's recollection.

highlights.text: Taichi: "You remember that, good."

adjudicated.jp: 「そうだよ。そーいう意味だ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "That's right. That was what it meant."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 今再び、同じ問いを投げかける。
adjudicated.en: And now, once again, I throw the same question at her.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「なあ霧……豊は、幸せだったのかな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Say, Kiri, I'm wondering... was Yutaka happy?"
comments: CP CCC3008
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ありがちな問いかけ。
adjudicated.en: An usual question to ask,
comments: CP CCC3008
adjudicated.assessment: The English article is wrong: 'usual' begins with a consonant sound and requires 'a,' not 'an.'

highlights.text: An usual question to ask,

adjudicated.jp: けど。
adjudicated.en: but,
comments: CP CCC3008
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 意味はまったく逆だった。
adjudicated.en: the meaning was wholly and damnably the opposite.
comments: CP CCC3008
adjudicated.assessment: The source describes the question as difficult to answer; the intensifier 'damnably' adds an unsupported profane register.

highlights.text: the meaning was wholly and damnably the opposite.

adjudicated.jp: 「……つらい思いをしてきたんです！」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...he was feeling bitter!"
comments: PCP CCC3008
adjudicated.assessment: 辛い目に遭ってきた refers to undergoing painful or harsh experiences. 'Had been feeling bitter' changes external suffering into an internal resentful attitude.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...he was feeling bitter!"

adjudicated.jp: 「親族に邪険にされて……荒れて……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "His relatives were so cruel... so rough..."
comments: Possibly referring to how they looked relieved at the funeral... possibly referring to the story in CCC3025. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says the person was badly treated by relatives and consequently became wild or troubled. 'Relatives were cruel, and so rough' leaves the result without its subject and makes 'rough' appear to modify the relatives.

highlights.text: Kiri: "His relatives were so cruel... so rough..."

adjudicated.jp: 「本当にずっとつらかった？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Truly, always, bitter?"
comments: CP CCC3008
adjudicated.assessment: The source again refers to experiencing painful or harsh treatment. 'Feeling so bitter' substitutes resentment for suffering.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Truly, always, bitter?"

adjudicated.jp: 「一瞬でも、幸せな時間はなかった？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "There were never times of happiness, not even one instant?"
comments: CP CCC3008
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「それは……」
adjudicated.en: Kiri: "Well..."
comments: CP CCC3008
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「あっただろうが」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I'm sure there were."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 霧は答えない。うつむく。
adjudicated.en: Kiri doesn't answer. And hangs her head.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 武器も下を向いている。
adjudicated.en: The weapon points down as well.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 敵意も殺意も萎んだ。枯れた花。
adjudicated.en: Hostility and murderous intent too wither. A wilted flower.
comments: SYMBOLISM!!! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 細い体に、疑念という毒素が満ちる。
adjudicated.en: Her thin slender body fills with a toxin named doubt.
comments: What toxin, this is a well needed medicine! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「そりゃそうだろうさ。昔しでかしたことを綺麗さっぱり忘れれば、心もスッキリサッパリだ。いくらだって幸せになれるさ！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Sooo, well, yeah, that's that. All the stuff he's done long ago is all beautifully and spotlessly forgotten, and his heart is all clean and refreshed. How so very happy could he become after that!"
comments: This is why forgetting's not removing the past, and why Taichi's attempt to have his way with the time loop can't work. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source concludes that once those memories are gone, the person can become as happy as can be. 'How so very happy could he become' is an ungrammatical question and loses the stated causal conclusion.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Sooo, well, yeah, that's that. All the stuff he's done long ago is all beautifully and spotlessly forgotten, and his heart is all clean and refreshed. How so very happy could he become after that!"

adjudicated.jp: 「だから思い出させてやった」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "And that is why I made him remember."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...stop this..."
comments: See CCD5001. It's not word for word, but it might as well be. And in both cases it's something they need to hear. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 霧は耳を塞ごうとする。
adjudicated.en: Kiri goes to cover her ears.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「塞ぐな！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Don't cover your ears!"
comments: Indeed. She can't run away from this. But see CCD3003B: she isn't. This entire thing is in Taichi's mind. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 手は止まる。
adjudicated.en: Hands stop.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「よく晴れた日だったよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "It was a nice clear sunny day."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「おまえが見たとおり、あの時の屋上ですべて話した」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "As you did see, that moment we talked about everything."
adjudicated.assessment: The speaker says that he told the other person everything on the rooftop at that time. 'That moment we talked about everything' removes the specified location and changes a one-way disclosure into mutual conversation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "As you did see, that moment we talked about everything."

adjudicated.en: Kiri: "...ngh..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「あいつは言った。どうすれば許してくれるって？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "And then he asked: how can I make you forgive me?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「許すも許さないもない。犯した罪は永遠にそのままだ。触れることなんてできない。変質させることもだ。俺もそこを責める気はなかった」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "There's no forgiving nor condemning. Sins perpetrated remain like that in eternity. There's no putting your hands on them in any way. Neither there is changing them. I didn't feel like there was blame then."
comments: And... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator says he never intended to blame the other person for the fixed facts. 'I didn't feel like there was blame then' removes both the narrator's agency and the object of blame; the preceding 'Neither there is changing them' is also ungrammatical.

highlights.text: Taichi: "There's no forgiving nor condemning. Sins perpetrated remain like that in eternity. There's no putting your hands on them in any way. Neither there is changing them. I didn't feel like there was blame then."

adjudicated.jp: 「……ただ、一つ疑問があってさ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...just, there was one thing unclear."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「問いかけたんだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "So I asked him a question:"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「なあ、ひとつ質問なんだけど……どうして今すぐにでも死なないんだ？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Say, I got one question though... why don't you just die right this very instant?"
comments: PCP CCC3009
This is one of the cornerstones of Cross Channel. The better question is: how come Yutaka didn't have another answer? -GHS

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 霧は崩れ落ちた。
adjudicated.en: Kiri crumbled down.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: その脇にしゃがみ込む。
adjudicated.en: She squats cradling her knees on the spot.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator crouches beside the seated person. 'She squats cradling her knees' assigns the movement and posture to the other person.

highlights.text: She squats cradling her knees on the spot.

adjudicated.jp: 俺の顔には、憫笑が刻まれている。
adjudicated.en: A smile of pity engraves on my face.
comments: But is it an insincere one? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: A pitying smile is etched on the person's face. 'A smile engraves' incorrectly makes the smile the agent of engraving and leaves the construction incomplete.

highlights.text: A smile of pity engraves on my face.

adjudicated.jp: 「いずれにせよ、真実は一つだけさ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "However things may go, the truth is only one:"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: あと一押しで、砕ける。
adjudicated.en: Just one more try, one more push, and she'll shatter.
comments: See CCA0026B. Since he's about to do a great big favor to her, I suspect this is intentional. Kiri's no more going to shatter than Misato is going to reject Taichi (provided he does it the way she wants it, i.e. giving her plausible deniability). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 知っているのに、俺は。
adjudicated.en: And I know that, but still,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 耳元に囁く。
adjudicated.en: I whisper in her ears,
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator whispers at one ear. The English plural 'ears' changes the concrete gesture.

highlights.text: I whisper in her ears,

adjudicated.jp: 本物の刃物を突き立てるために。
adjudicated.en: so as to stab her with the blade of a weapon with a real edge.
comments: Because of the vagaries of Kiri's knife etc., this will return in CCX0001. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「おまえの兄さんは薄汚い最低のレイプ猿だ」

comments: "Rapist monkey" or "rapist chimp" sound a tad too silly, though it connects to how Touko calls him a monkey in heat. Outside of that it's not used literally anyway, and as I can't think of an animal that wouldn't sort of blunt this (like 'dog'), I fucking need to fucking go with another fucking swearword, mother of all shitfuck. -GHShitfuck
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.
The source text has multiple authoritative occurrences and this unit lacks a unique binding.

adjudicated.jp: プツン、と。
adjudicated.en: Snap.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 霧の内部で糸が切れるのがわかった。
adjudicated.en: And so I knew that a string inside Kiri had been cut,
adjudicated.assessment: The metaphorical string snapped or broke. 'Had been cut' implies an external cutting agent and changes the event into an earlier past-perfect action.

highlights.text: And so I knew that a string inside Kiri had been cut,

adjudicated.jp: 決してもう繋がるまい。
adjudicated.en: and may never be reconnected again.
comments: The one that binds her to Yutaka. This is a GOOD THING FOR HER. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: きっと二度と繋がらない expresses the speaker's firm expectation that it will surely never reconnect. 'May never' weakens this to possibility.

highlights.text: and may never be reconnected again.
